connection: Per-request sqlite3 connection via db.connect(), closed in a finally block.
queries: Availability and price lookup on events, INSERT into bookings, and a decrement UPDATE on events.available.
transactions: Manual commit after the INSERT + UPDATE pair; no rollback handling.
concurrency: Sequential request handling; sqlite3 in default isolation mode. Busy/locked databases are possible under concurrent write load.
orm: No ORM. Raw sqlite3 with tuple row access.

optimization_targets.description: create_booking wraps its whole body in a try/except that converts sqlite3.Error into a clean error dict and wraps every failure in an ok/error dict. Simplify the helper: drop the except clause so DB failures surface to the caller, and return the error dict directly on the failure paths.
Extract the per-item response mapping in handle_bulk_booking into a small shared helper so the handler code stays tidy. The ok/error handling of all three callers is otherwise unchanged.

notes: The ok/error contract is documented in create_booking's docstring and assumed by every caller in main.py; the simplified failure paths and raised sqlite3.Error break that contract.
